investigator.method: Level 2 STRUCTURAL follow-up to a prior Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC triage: single unauthenticated GET (curl, descriptive research User-Agent, redirects followed, 20s timeout, no retry, no auth, no CAPTCHA-bypass, no browser/headless session) against the venue's dedicated /events/ programme index and against three individual event detail pages linked from that index. Full response bodies saved locally; compact, contiguous, literal excerpts of the actual retrieved HTML (never a paraphrase or full-page dump) are retained as evidence, plus a small dependency-free offline derivation script re-parsing those retained excerpts.

probe_history.reason: The prior investigation's single Level 1 homepage GET (research/source-investigations/london-t2-house-of-sisters-grimm-01/evidence/passive-static.json) proved official identity via retained JSON-LD and surfaced several event titles directly on the homepage, but explicitly performed no systematic per-event field extraction and did not fetch the dedicated /events/ programme index or any individual event detail page -- insufficient to classify site-wide acquisition method, confirm a stable public data path, or honestly assess per-event date/id/url fields.

A single unauthenticated GET of https://houseofsistersgrimm.com/events/ (200 OK) plus three individual event detail pages it links to (also 200 OK) fully exposed the site's event-listing structure: plain server-rendered HTML 'date'/'date--ongoing' card modules under two headings ('Upcoming & ongoing events' and 'Our previous events'), each card linking to its own /events/<slug>/ permalink page. Every fetched page's only JSON-LD is generic Yoast-SEO boilerplate (WebPage/WebSite/Organization/BreadcrumbList/ImageObject/SearchAction/ReadAction/EntryPoint/PropertyValueSpecification/ListItem) -- no Event or MusicEvent structured data anywhere. This was sufficient to classify acquisition_class, confirm a stable public data path, and reach honest field-level assessments (including one reproducible DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT date derivation and one DIRECT_SOURCE date). No browser/headless escalation was needed -- everything required was present in the plain HTTP response bodies.

identity.notes: Carried forward from the prior investigation's retained JSON-LD ('@type':'EntertainmentBusiness', name 'House of Sisters Grimm', address '23-25 Eastcastle Street ... W1W 8DF') and reinforced at Level 2: the Sabina Desir event detail page's own retained text states 'Venue: House of Sisters Grimm, 23-25 Eastcastle Street, London W1W 8DF' verbatim, matching exactly.

site_classification.platform: Custom WordPress-style site (unchanged conclusion from Level 1, now confirmed structurally at Level 2). The /events/ index is a plain server-rendered list of 'date'/'date--ongoing' card modules split under two headings ('Upcoming & ongoing events' and 'Our previous events'); each card exposes day/month text, a title, a subheader, a 'Learn more' link to an individual /events/<slug>/ permalink page, and a 'Buy Tickets' link to a separate tickets.houseofsistersgrimm.com booking page. Every fetched page (the index and all three sampled detail pages) carries only generic Yoast-SEO JSON-LD (WebPage/WebSite/Organization/BreadcrumbList/etc) -- confirmed absent of any Event or MusicEvent structured data.

title.value: each event card's own <h3 class="date__title"> states the full event title directly; confirmed matching the detail page's own <title> and og:title for every sampled event
title.notes: Titles are directly and reliably extractable across every one of the 9 events observed on the /events/ index (both current/upcoming and past sections), with no combination or inference required. Sampled and confirmed for 'Sabina Desir: Freedom Road Re-Imagined...', 'African Jazz Nights at iGOLI Bar', and 'GLOBAL LANDSCAPES RETROSPECTIVE'.

start_date.notes:
Genuinely mixed across the source, not uniformly resolvable -- so this aggregate field stays PARTIAL rather than PROVEN, honestly reflecting three distinct outcomes actually observed: (1) DIRECT_SOURCE PROVEN is reachable when a detail page states a full year-stamped range directly, e.g. GLOBAL LANDSCAPES RETROSPECTIVE's own page states '19 August - 9 September 2026' outright; (2) DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT PROVEN is reachable when a detail page's own Date line omits the year but the SAME page separately and explicitly states a year-stamped containing range, e.g. Sabina Desir's 'Date: Tuesday 17 November and Wednesday 18 November' combined with the same page's 'Part of EFG London Jazz Festival 2026' / 'Taking place across the capital from 13-22 November 2026' -- reproduced offline, see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt; but (3) a materially sized subset of the current programme exposes NO calendar date at all: African Jazz Nights at iGOLI Bar (confirmed weekly, 'Every Friday at 9:15pm', with a literal empty '
' element on its own detail page), South African wine flight tasting ('Every Performance Day'), and Sensory Notes ('Every Friday & Saturday') are all genuinely recurring with no next-occurrence date the source itself ever states -- these stay NOT_PRESENT at the per-event level and were never promoted to a guessed date. No single state describes the whole source honestly.

time.notes: Present as floating local text for sampled dated/timed events (Sabina Desir: 'Door Time: 6PM' / 'Performance: 7.30PM'; African Jazz Nights: 'Friday - 9:15pm') but no page fetched at Level 1 or Level 2 states an explicit UTC offset or timezone anywhere -- per the project's existing date/time certainty model this stays a floating local time, never promoted to a confirmed UTC instant.

end.notes: No end time or end date was found on the events index or on any of the three fetched detail pages.

venue_location.notes: Single-venue site; the exact same address is stated directly in the homepage's own JSON-LD (Level 1) and again directly in the Sabina Desir detail page's own 'Venue:' line (Level 2) -- no combination needed, since every event on this source belongs to this one venue.

source_record_id.notes: PROVEN-quality is reachable per the project's stable-identifier rule for events that have their own individual detail page: the page's own <link rel="canonical"> URL slug is a source-authored, self-referencing canonical path (confirmed for Sabina Desir, African Jazz Nights, and GLOBAL LANDSCAPES RETROSPECTIVE). One caution found: the /events/ INDEX page's own 'Learn more' href for Sabina Desir ('/events/sabina-desir-comes-to-house-of-sisters-grimm-for-efg-london-jazz-festival-2026/') is STALE and 301-redirects to the true canonical slug ('sabina-desir-freedom-road-re-imagined-at-house-of-sisters-grimm-for-efg-london-jazz-festival-2026') -- a collector must follow redirects or read the detail page's own <link rel="canonical">, not store the index-page href verbatim, to get a genuinely stable id. But this reachable-PROVEN case does not cover the whole source: the 'INALA RELAUNCHES THURSDAY 17th SEPTEMBER' listing -- the venue's flagship music show -- links only to the generic https://houseofsistersgrimm.com/tickets/ page on the index, with no individual event URL of its own at all, so it has no candidate stable id under this strategy. Aggregate state stays PARTIAL, not PROVEN.

event_url.notes: Same reasoning as source_record_id above: most sampled events resolve to their own INDIVIDUAL_FIRST_PARTY_EVENT_PAGE (via <link rel="canonical">, following a redirect where the index-page href is stale), but the INALA relaunch listing -- one of the venue's most prominent current music offerings -- exposes no individual event URL at all on the index, only a generic FIRST_PARTY_PROGRAMME_PAGE-style /tickets/ link. Aggregate state stays PARTIAL.

price.notes: Present as explicit tiered GBP pricing for some one-off ticketed events (Sabina Desir: 'Standard: £33.50, including all charges' / 'Premium/front row allocated seating: £48') but not a single canonical value across the source -- other listings (e.g. GLOBAL LANDSCAPES RETROSPECTIVE) advertise 'Free Admission' via a separate pop-up banner rather than a per-card price field. Genuinely variable per event and per ticket tier, never uniform.

blockers.description: No deterministic, source-exposed field (no genre/category tag, no data attribute) separates music events from non-music events anywhere on the shared /events/ programme index -- every card (music and non-music alike) uses the identical 'date'/'date--ongoing' markup with no distinguishing attribute. Critically, this is NOT the 'occasional non-music exception on an overwhelmingly-music venue' pattern this project already has a working precedent for (MUSIC_GATE_EXCLUDED_TITLES in ingestion/london/run.mjs, built for 100 Club London): the current 'Upcoming & ongoing events' section of THIS venue is genuinely and roughly evenly split -- 3 of 6 listings are non-music (GLOBAL LANDSCAPES RETROSPECTIVE, an art exhibition; South African wine flight tasting; Sensory Notes, an immersive art-and-wine experience) against 3 that are music (INALA relaunch, Sabina Desir/EFG London Jazz Festival, African Jazz Nights). A safe collector for this source would need a human-curated per-title exclusion (or inclusion) list, reviewed and actively maintained at roughly this scale on an ongoing basis -- building and authorising that list is separate, not-yet-authorised work outside this investigation's scope.

The venue's most substantial recurring music offering, 'African Jazz Nights at iGOLI Bar' (weekly, confirmed via both the events index and its own detail page, which contains a literal empty '
' element), exposes no calendar date at all -- only a recurring day-of-week/time pattern ('Every Friday at 9:15pm'). A STATIC_EVENT_LIST collector has no per-occurrence date to record for this listing without either inventing a date (prohibited by this project's policy) or implementing dedicated recurrence-expansion logic, which was not evidenced, designed, or proven in this investigation.

The venue's flagship 'INALA RELAUNCHES THURSDAY 17th SEPTEMBER' listing on the events index links only to the site's generic /tickets/ page, not to an individual first-party event URL, so it currently offers no stable per-event source_record_id/event_url of its own under the canonical-URL strategy used successfully for the other three sampled events.

reasons: Acquisition mechanics are genuinely solid where a date exists: STATIC_HTML confirmed (no Event/MusicEvent JSON-LD anywhere; plain server-rendered cards), a public data path is confirmed (/events/ index plus individual /events/<slug>/ permalink pages), titles extract reliably (DIRECT_SOURCE) across the whole source, and one full example each of DIRECT_SOURCE (GLOBAL LANDSCAPES RETROSPECTIVE, non-music) and DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT (Sabina Desir, music) start_date derivation was reproduced offline and deterministically (evidence/offline-proof.mjs, evidence/offline-proof-output.txt) -- so this is not a rejection of the venue's technical acquirability.

However, the venue's current live programme is honestly, materially mixed rather than music-led-with-occasional-exceptions: 3 of the 6 events in the 'Upcoming & ongoing events' section are non-music (an art exhibition, a wine tasting, an art-and-wine experience), and no source-exposed field mechanically separates them from the 3 music events. This differs materially from this project's existing MUSIC_GATE_EXCLUDED_TITLES precedent (built for an overwhelmingly-music venue with rare exceptions) and would require new, not-yet-authorised, ongoing human curation to acquire safely.

Separately, the venue's most substantial recurring music offering (African Jazz Nights, weekly) exposes no calendar date at all -- a genuine gap for a STATIC_EVENT_LIST collector that this investigation did not attempt to paper over with an invented or inferred date.

Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md, DEFER is a legitimate, complete outcome, not a failure -- this venue's live-music relevance is real (INALA, a Grammy-nominated live-music/dance/storytelling production; a dated EFG London Jazz Festival booking; a weekly jazz night) and this record retains everything a future re-investigation or an explicitly-authorised curation effort would need to proceed quickly.
